name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years. This second season sees the invaders firmly entrenched in their assault, advanced to the great cities of the Iron Kingdoms but ground to a stalemate by the grit and will of the defending armies. The impasse will be short-lived, however, as strange circumstances make for strange allies, and new forces join the struggle for the future of the Iron Kingdoms!

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player chooses to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games as the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Character warjacks cannot be used in this campaign through normal army construction. Instead, they are created progressively by upgrading a preset warjack through with War Chest points (see below).

name: Name
body: Over the course of the Black Tide campaign, players will receive and track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles described at the end of each scenario. Beginning in Season Two, War Chest points may be spent between matches on a variety of benefits. Each player will be responsible for keeping a ledger of their own War Chest points. Be sure to add any War Chest points gained during a match to your total after the match and take care to accurately subtract the appropriate War Chest points from your total when you spend them for any benefits. A printable War Chest tracking sheet can be downloaded at Black Tide Season 2 War Chest Record Sheet

name: Name
body: There are three ways to spend your War Chest points during the course of the campaign: Strategic Advantages, Campaign Command Cards, and Character Warjack Upgrades.

name: Name
body:
Players can spend up to 4 War Chest points before a match for Strategic Advantages that provide a benefit during the course of the match. A Strategic Advantage is only good for the match you buy it for and does not carry over into subsequent matches.
Some Strategic Advantages can only be taken by the Underdog in match. The Underdog is the player who has the fewest War Chest points going into the match. If players are tied with War Chest points, there is no Underdog.
Normal Strategic Advantages cost 2 War Chest points. Underdog Advantages cost 1 War Chest point. Strategic Advantages can be added to your force list after Creating a Match in the WARMACHINE app by tapping the ADVANTAGES button at the bottom of the card list.

name: Name
body:
Campaign Command Cards are Command Cards designed specifically for use in the Black Tide campaign and are not meant for play in non-campaign games. Campaign Command Cards must be unlocked for use by paying 3 War Chest points. Once unlocked, they can be used in any subsequent game. Note that some Campaign Command Cards also have army point costs like other Command Cards.
Be sure to record any Campaign Command Cards you unlock so you know what is available to your force in later matches.
Campaign Command Cards will appear in your normal Command Card list in the WARMACHINE app and can be identified by the presence of "[CAMPAIGN]" in the title of the card.

name: Name
body:
In the Black Tide campaign, players using MKIV armies can use War Chest points to upgrade character warjacks. Character warjacks start with a stock loadout and can be upgraded over time by spending War Chest points. Each upgrade costs 3 War Chest points, and once an upgrade is purchased, it is a permanent change to the warjack for all subsequent matches. The benefit to upgrading a character warjack in this fashion is that the upgrades do not change the army point cost of the warjack, so as you upgrade it, the warjack gets a more valuable loadout, which is then permanently available to your force at a bargain cost.
When upgrading a character warjack, both arm weapons must be upgraded before the head can be upgraded. And the head must be upgraded before a bond can be selected. Once an upgrade is purchased, including a bond, it cannot be changed for the duration of the campaign.
Be sure to record your character warjack upgrades when you spend your War Chest points on them.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective uncontested.

name: Name
body: Scenario victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set number of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle scenario gains an additional War Chest point.
Players who are participating in the Resurrection League may choose to include the league model, Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, as part of their force. If they do, they may undertake a Gobber Spy mission during the Key Battles of this campaign to earn additional Victory Points. Gobber Spy missions are detailed in the Key Battle scenarios.

name: Name
body: The bitter winds of winter howled across the war-torn landscape of the Rustoknia territory, carrying with them the promise of an unforgiving season that would test the mettle of both the Motherland’s defenders and the relentless Orgoth invaders. As the first flakes of snow drifted down from the slate-gray sky, a palpable sense of anticipation hung heavy in the air. Khador had seen its fair share of brutal conflicts, but this winter promised a wrath unlike any other. The war had raged on for months, with the Khadorans locked in the desperate struggle to protect their homeland from the dreaded Orgoth forces. The barbaric invaders had pushed deep into Rustoknia during their siege of Khardov, leaving a wake of destruction through the Blackroot Forest. But as the temperature dropped and the snow began to blanket the land, it became clear that the onset of winter would bring a drastic shift in the dynamics of the conflict. The Khadorans, renowned for their resilience and unwavering determination, saw the encroaching winter as both a blessing and a curse. On one hand, the snow-covered terrain would hinder the Orgoth advance, slowing their war machines and making it more difficult for their forces to maneuver. On the other hand, the harsh conditions would also test the already beleaguered Winter Korps’ ability to hold their ground and maintain their supply lines.

name: Name
body: Kommander Savaryn stood atop a rime-covered hill overlooking the front lines. His breath formed a frosty cloud in the frigid air as he surveyed the scene below. His troops were hard at work, fortifying their positions and digging trenches to provide cover from the biting cold and enemy fire that would soon return. The sounds of hammers striking steel and the shouts of orders echoed across the wintry landscape. Savaryn knew that the coming months would be a grueling test of endurance. Despite their inexperience with the Khadoran winter, the Orgoth raiders were not to be underestimated. They were a merciless and unyielding opponent whose willingness to sacrifice anything and everything in the pursuit of their objectives had become a humbling and frightening subject among the Khadoran ranks. As the first true snowfall of winter began to intensify, Savaryn turned his attention to the sky. The flakes fell steadily, blanketing the land in a pristine white sheet. It was a cruel beauty, a stark contrast to the violence and chaos of war. But beneath that blanket of snow waited a deadly battlefield, and the coming months would determine more than just the fate of the Khadoran Empire.

name: Name
body: The war for the Iron Kingdoms had entered a new and treacherous phase, one in which the elements themselves would become a formidable adversary. Kommander Savaryn tightened his grip on his mechanika blade and prepared to lead his troops into the icy crucible of winter warfare, where every decision, every maneuver, would be critical to their survival. Black Tide Season 3, Chapter 2 is made up of three scenarios that should be played in order: "Thin Ice," "Shipwrecked," and "Snowfall."

name: Name
body: In the chill heart of winter, after a night of heavy snowfall, enemy forces lock eyes across a vast, snow-covered expanse. The tension in the air thickens as they both realize the cruel twist of fate: their impending battle is about to unfold upon the treacherous surface of a frozen lake, its icy depths concealed beneath a thin veneer of snow. The winds whisper an ominous warning, for in this battle, the very ground beneath their feet will become yet another merciless and unpredictable adversary.

name: Name
body:
Despite the snows and the bitter bite of winter, the war goes on. With both sides entrenched behind their barricades of earth and ice, patrols are dispatched into the no man’s land between to probe the defenses of the enemy. Sometimes these patrolling forces meet, and then the grounds they mutually traverse erupt into dangerous battlefields…especially when both sides are walking on thin ice.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: Each player builds a 50-point army.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, the battlefield should be divided into six 16" x 24" objective zones.
A 36" diameter frozen lake sits in the middle of the table. The frozen lake has the following special rules:
Models without Flight, Ghostly, Incorporeal, or Pathfinder beginning a charge, run, slam power attack, or trample power attack while completely within the area of the frozen lake must make a Slip Roll before moving.
Models without Flight, Ghostly, Incorporeal, or Pathfinder that begin a charge, run, slam power attack, or trample power attack and end their movement completely within the area of the lake must make a Slip Roll at the end of their movement.
When a model is directly hit by an AOE attack and/or an attack that causes fire damage while completely within the area of the frozen lake, after the attack has been completely resolved, the model must make a Slip Roll.
When a model must make a Slip Roll, roll a d6. On the roll of 1, the model becomes knocked down. On any other roll, nothing happens.

name: Name
body:
When a Cohort model becomes knocked down for any reason while on the frozen lake, it breaks through the ice, suffers d6 damage points, and becomes stationary for one round instead of becoming knocked down.
Players then take turns placing up to three additional terrain features each. Players cannot place terrain feature within 4" of another terrain feature, but terrain can be placed on the frozen lake.  Buildings, however, cannot be placed within the area of the frozen lake. Players cannot place Fire Pit or Spike Trap defenses within the area of the frozen lake.
Players roll off to start the game normally. The first player takes the first turn, and the second player has their choice of table edges to deploy to. The first player then deploys their forces within 7" of the opposite edge. The second player deploys their forces within 10" of their table edge.

name: Name
body: A player scores 1 Victory Point for each objective zone they secure at the beginning of each of their turns beginning with the first player’s second turn.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If either player begins a turn securing all three objective zones on their opponent’s side of the table, that player wins the match and gains 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: Amidst the relentless grip of winter, weary and famished soldiers gather at a frozen riverbank, their eyes fixed upon the remains of a merchant vessel run aground. The promise of salvation lies within its battered hull—a trove of precious supplies to stave off hunger and death. But their resolve is matched by that of the enemy, whose shadowy figures advance through the snow. With frostbitten fingers clenched around their weapons, these warriors prepare to wage war over the shipwreck’s vital bounty, for in the heart of winter, survival comes at the cost of blood and steel.

name: Name
body:
As the winter months linger on, supplies to the frontlines often dwindle. With belts tightening, no spare resources can be ignored. When a recent shipwreck laden with food and raw materials is discovered spanning a nearby river, both camps rush to claim any goods they can get their hands on. As both sides meet in battle, their generals wonder how long the calm in the tumultuous winter weather will hold.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 75- and 100-point armies.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, an 8"-wide river spans the middle of the battlefield. The river is difficult terrain. Models that move, are moved, or are placed completely within the area of the river are removed from play. This does not include models with Flight, Incorporeal, or Ghostly.
Place a 6" x 10" shipwreck objective diagonally across the center of the river so that it spans both sides of the river equally. The shipwreck objective is an obstruction.
A 6"-wide bridge spans the river 8" from the east table edge. Models completely on the bridge gain cover from arcane and ranged attacks made by models not completely on the bridge.
Players then take turns placing up to five additional terrain features each. A player cannot place a terrain feature within 4" of another terrain feature, including the river, bridge, and shipwreck objective.
Players roll off to start the game normally. The first player takes the first turn, and the second player has their choice of the north or south table edge to deploy to. The first player then deploys their forces within 7" of the opposite edge. The second player deploys their forces within 10" of their table edge.

name: Name
body:
Unpredictable Winter Weather: At the start of each player’s turn, roll a d6. On the roll of 1 or 2, a storm either starts or ends. On a roll of 3-6, nothing happens.
When a storm begins, roll 1d6 on the table below:
1-2:
Obscuring Mists: All models gain concealment. Additionally, the LOS of all models is limited to 12".
3:
Heavy Winds: All models suffer –1 SPD, MAT, and RAT. Additionally, all models lose Flight.
4:
Cold Snap: Models without Resistance: Cold suffer –1 DEF and cannot make Tough rolls.
5:
Ice Storm: All models gain concealment. Additionally, warrior models without Resistance: Cold that do not move at least 1" or are not placed during their activations suffer a POW 10 damage roll.
6:
Blizzard: All models treat open terrain as rough terrain and gain concealment. Additionally, the LOS of all models is limited to 10".
Storms continue until a player rolls a 1 or 2 at the start of their turn to end it. The storm’s effects expire when the storm ends. Once a storm ends, there is always a chance a new storm will begin at the beginning of the next player’s next turn.

name: Name
body:
A Cohort model in base contact with the shipwreck objective during its activation can make a special action to gain a cargo token. A Cohort model can only have one cargo token at any time. When a Cohort model gains a cargo token, its controlling player scores 1 Victory Point.
When a Cohort model with a cargo token begins its activation completely within the area of its controlling player’s deployment zone, remove the cargo token from the model and its controlling player scores 2 Victory Points.
A player securing the shipwreck objective at the start of each of their turns scores 1 Victory Point.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If either player has three or more cargo tokens removed from their Cohort models while in their deployment zone, that player wins the match and gains 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: For months, opposing forces have stared each other down across a frozen battlefield, their resolve unbroken in the harsh embrace of winter. But as a bone-chilling blizzard rages, the fragile peace shatters. The howling storm creates an almost impenetrable veil as soldiers emerge from their snow-covered trenches, driven by the unyielding call of battle amidst the whiteout. In the heart of the bitter tempest, amidst the icy chaos, a desperate clash erupts as both sides are unwilling to yield even an inch of the snow-clad battleground.

name: Name
body:
As the winter months wear on, both sides expand their earthworks, slowly cutting new trenches into the hard, frozen ground. With both entrenched forces separated by a scant dozen or so feet, a fierce battle suddenly breaks out between them as heavy snow falls overhead.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 75- and 100-point armies.

name: Name
body:
Players roll off to determine the first player. The first player deploys first and takes the first turn.
Each player should place a 3" x 5" command trench in the middle of their deployment zone, touching the farthest edge of their deployment zone as shown on the map below. Then players take turns each placing four additional 3" x 5" trenches on their side of the table outside their deployment zones, beginning with the first player.
Players then take turns placing up to four additional non-trench terrain features each.A player also cannot place these terrain features within 4" of another terrain feature.

name: Name
body:
Lay of the Land: The models of the player who lost the Thin Ice scenario lose Advance Deployment and Ambush when playing this scenario.
Combat Ready: The healthy and hale warrior models of the player who won the Shipwrecked scenario gain Tough during the first two rounds of the game.
Falling Snow: Snow falls throughout the battle, gradually getting heavier as the conflict rages on. At the start of each player’s turn, beginning with the first player’s second turn, roll a d6. On the roll of a 1, the storm worsens to the next Stage. On any other roll, nothing happens.
The storm is at Stage 1 at the beginning of the game.
The effects of the storm stages are:
Stage 1: All models gain concealment.
Stage 2: All models gain concealment. Models treat open terrain as rough terrain.
Stage 3: All models gain concealment. Models treat open terrain as rough terrain. Models lose Flight. All models have their LOS reduced to 12".
Stage 4: All models gain concealment. Models treat open terrain as rough terrain. Models lose Flight. All models have their LOS reduced to 12". Models without Resistance: Cold suffer –1 DEF and lose Tough.

name: Name
body:
Gobber Spy Mission: Players who include Reinholdt, Gobber Spy in their force can undertake the following covert mission:
- Gather Intel: Reinholdt, Gobber Spy can make the Gather Intel special action once per game while within the area of your opponent’s command trench. When he does so, you gain 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body: A player scores 1 Victory Point for each trench objective on their opponent’s side of the table they are holding at the beginning of each of their turns.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, if a player is holding their opponent’s command trench, they win the match and receive 6 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.
